v.rationale: All three pass their own test suites. All three walk primary-key ranges, fill only NULL customer_id rows, and update through the query builder so updated_at doesn't change. I probed id gaps, chunk size 1, re-running after a customer is deleted, and updated_at preservation, and those all work in every implementation. What separates them is the endpoint and the schema details. A probe of `?status=` (empty value) shows that impl-2 and impl-3 both added a FormRequest with 'sometimes','string' and no 'nullable'. Laravel's ConvertEmptyStringsToNull turns the empty value into null, so the endpoint now returns 422 where the base app returned all orders. That is a regression on the frequently called endpoint, and the task never asked for validation. impl-1 kept the original behaviour. On the schema side, impl-1 and impl-2 both add the column INSTANT, build the two indexes INPLACE/LOCK=NONE (one for the filtered query, one for the unfiltered query and the FK), and add the FK INPLACE with FK checks off. impl-2 does it with Laravel 13's first-class ->instant()/->inplace()/->lock() modifiers in three retryable migrations, which is more idiomatic than impl-1's raw SQL with a separate branch for non-MySQL drivers. impl-3 gives no algorithm or lock guarantees, uses a positional after() column, and has only one index, so the unfiltered listing has to filesort. Ranking: impl-1 first (correct and safe, a bit raw), impl-2 second (best framework idioms but an API regression), impl-3 third (the same regression plus weaker indexing and migration safety). I had no MySQL server to run against, so the MySQL DDL was checked by compiling the migrations, not by executing them. All probe tests were deleted afterwards.
